A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same study, Demystifying Mergeability, with complete main text and Appendices A.1–A.9. Text extraction and visual inspection support comparison of the equations, figures and tables across both versions.

before.justification: v1 reports original mergeability-prediction experiments on 190 pairs of models covering 20 image-classification tasks, including cross-validation results, predictor comparisons, ablations and regularized fine-tuning results.

after.justification: v4 retains these original empirical results, including the main cross-validation results in Table 2 and the supplementary experiments in the appendices.

M1.justification: Appendix A.5.2, Equation 7, replaces a penalty on squared distance from pretrained weights with a penalty on squared cross-entropy-gradient magnitudes. This substantially revises the stated objective of the supplementary fine-tuning method; the central 28-metric linear predictor remains unchanged. Because v1 already describes gradient-magnitude regularization elsewhere, the PDFs do not establish whether implementation changed or the description was corrected.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same 20 image-classification tasks and pairwise merging scenarios, including the regularization experiment. Appendix A.9 retains the same dataset coverage; no additional domains, populations or task requirements appear.

E2.justification: The same four merging methods are studied: Task Arithmetic, Weight Averaging, Isotropic Merging and TSV. The MLP comparison in Table 6, baseline fine-tuning comparison in Table 12 and unregularized-versus-Lasso comparison in Table 13 retain their comparator sets.

E3.justification: The 190 model pairs, 20-fold leave-one-task-out evaluation, normalization, calibration sample counts and experimental hyperparameters remain unchanged. Appendix A.5 retains the same three regularization strengths, 0.001, 0.1 and 1; apart from its revised method objective, no separate evaluation-protocol change is reported.

E4.justification: The existing merge-aware fine-tuning case study in Appendix A.5 specifies a different intervention: penalizing loss gradients instead of displacement from pretrained weights. This is a limited revision to the documented regularization study, without new supporting results. The individual-metric, MLP, Lasso and metric-category ablations remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Fold counts, reported means and standard deviations, significance conventions and calibration seeds remain unchanged. Section 6.3 removes a reference to examining standard deviations, but both versions define stable metrics through signs of fold-mean coefficients and retain the coefficient uncertainty in Table 9; no changed uncertainty-estimation procedure is established.

E6.justification: Introduction contribution 3 changes the reported correlation range from [0.34, 0.61] to [0.34, 0.57], correcting its upper endpoint to match TSV's 0.572 in the unchanged Table 2. Numerical tables and plotted results otherwise remain unchanged, including Table 12's average improvement of +0.55. The revised regularizer description therefore does not demonstrate a new performance gain.

T1.justification: Equation 7 substantively changes the mathematical definition of the supplementary training objective: parameter displacement and loss-gradient magnitude are different quantities. The predictor objective, cross-validation formalization and mergeability-metric definitions remain unchanged, with no new theorem or proof.

C1.justification: The introduction slightly narrows the quantitative prediction claim by lowering its upper correlation bound from 0.61 to 0.57. The central contributions—method- and partner-dependent mergeability, interpretable success fingerprints, shared gradient/subspace signals and actionable fine-tuning guidance—remain unchanged.

C2.justification: Appendix A.5.1 removes the assertion that gradient alignment is equivalent to similarity of accumulated parameter updates. Its mechanism explanation changes from directly constraining proximity to pretrained weights to discouraging large gradients and encouraging gradual updates. The applicability limitations and acknowledged absence of single-task performance evaluation remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Appendix A.8 and Tables 15–20 retain the same implementation settings, including optimizers, learning rates, batch sizes, calibration layers, precision, clipping and dataset-specific epochs. No additional implementation procedure or resource-access information accompanies the revised objective; Table 20 is relocated without changing its contents.

R1.justification: The cited works and research positioning remain unchanged. The references for On Task Vectors and Gradients and ATM are updated from preprint descriptions to publication venues, representing bibliographic updates rather than new related work or a changed novelty argument.

P1.justification: There are localized rewrites in Section 6.3 and Appendix A.5, alongside quotation, caption-wording, date and bibliography edits. The overall narrative and section organization remain intact. Appendix A.5.5 also acquires an unresolved '(?)' citation.

P2.justification: The figures and tables are retained, with limited caption editing and appendix reflow. Table 20 moves from page 26 to page 27, Table 19 is repositioned, and several paragraphs and the A.7 heading shift across page boundaries. There is no substantial visual redesign.

improvement.justification: v4 modestly improves precision and internal consistency: Equation 7 now matches the existing gradient-magnitude description, the gradient/update equivalence assertion is removed, and the introduction's upper correlation bound matches Table 2. These gains are limited by unchanged empirical evidence and the lack of an explanation connecting the revised objective to the identical Table 12 results. The new unresolved citation is a small presentation regression.
